You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From ee3be3c8eb97b6d56b8266cb02fc976e468641ea Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tad Hunt <tad@exablox.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2015 14:23:17 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] fix Apple OSX build issue

Fix build issue introduced by commit 9b0b8c1cbd1d945fb096d6130f18c99ca901e567
"Local variable names shadowed global function names (e.g. read),
this would cause compile errors with gcc 4.4.7."
---
 src/lib/kinetic_socket.c | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/src/lib/kinetic_socket.c b/src/lib/kinetic_socket.c
index 96ff7d33..a229e7d6 100644
--- a/src/lib/kinetic_socket.c
+++ b/src/lib/kinetic_socket.c
@@ -165,7 +165,7 @@ void KineticSocket_BeginPacket(int fd)
     int on = 1;
     setsockopt(fd, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_CORK, &on, sizeof(on));
 #else
-    (void)socket;
+    (void)fd;
 #endif
 }
 
@@ -175,6 +175,6 @@ void KineticSocket_FinishPacket(int fd)
     int off = 0;
     setsockopt(fd, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_CORK, &off, sizeof(off));
 #else
-    (void)socket;
+    (void)fd;
 #endif
 }
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by local variable names in the code that shadowed global function names, specifically the variable `socket` which conflicted with the global function `socket()`. This shadowing led to compile errors with GCC version 4.4.7, particularly on Apple OSX, as the compiler could not resolve the correct reference to the global function due to the local variable having the same name. The patch resolves this issue by changing the local variable name from `socket` to `fd`, thereby eliminating the name conflict and allowing the code to compile successfully.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by local variable names in the code that shadowed global function names, specifically the variable `socket` which conflicted with the global function `socket()`. This shadowing led to compile errors with GCC version 4.4.7, particularly on Apple OSX, as the compiler could not resolve the correct reference to the global function due to the local variable having the same name. The patch resolves this issue by changing the local variable name from `socket` to `fd`, thereby eliminating the name conflict and allowing the code to compile successfully.
